paragraphs.title: A Call to Praise and the Choice of Israel

easy.explanation: Verse 1 calls the servants of the LORD to praise His name.
easy.q: Whom does the psalm call to praise the name of the LORD?

answers: In the house of the LORD and the courts of the house of God
easy.explanation: Verse 2 says they stand in the house of the LORD and in His courts.
easy.q: Where do the servants of the LORD stand?

easy.explanation: Verse 4 says the LORD chose Jacob and Israel for His peculiar treasure.
easy.q: Whom did the LORD choose for His peculiar treasure?

answers: Because the LORD is good and His name is pleasant
Because they had won a battle
Because He had given them kings
medium.explanation: Verse 3 gives the LORD’s goodness and the pleasantness of His name as reasons for praise.
medium.q: Why are the servants of the LORD called to sing praises unto His name?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes Israel as a people specially chosen and treasured by the LORD.
medium.q: What does the phrase “peculiar treasure” mean in this passage?

answers: Those who stand in His house are called to praise Him
Those in His house must go to war
Those in His house receive the nations’ lands
medium.explanation: The people standing in the LORD’s house are directly called to praise His name.
medium.q: How are standing in the LORD’s house and praising Him connected?

answers: War, victory, and the division of land
Praise, the goodness of the LORD, and the choice of Israel
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from a call to praise to the LORD’s goodness and His choice of Jacob and Israel.
challenge.q: What sequence of ideas appears in verses 1–4?

answers: That they are His special people
That they rule over every nation
challenge.explanation: Israel is described as the LORD’s peculiar treasure.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the LORD’s choice of Jacob and Israel?

answers: His goodness and the pleasantness of His name
challenge.explanation: The verse says, “the LORD is good” and “it is pleasant” to sing praises unto His name.
challenge.q: Which quality of the LORD is given as a reason for praise in verse 3?

paragraphs.title: The LORD’s Greatness in Creation and Nature

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “I know that the LORD is great.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist say that he knows?

answers: In heaven, earth, the seas, and all deep places
easy.explanation: Verse 6 lists heaven, earth, the seas, and all deep places.
easy.q: Where does the LORD do whatsoever He pleases?

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says He causes the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth.
easy.q: What does the LORD cause to ascend from the ends of the earth?

answers: He makes lightnings, brings rain, and brings the wind
He builds cities by human hands
He chooses the kings of the nations
medium.explanation: Verse 7 attributes vapours, lightning, rain, and wind to the LORD.
medium.q: How is the LORD’s rule over nature shown in this passage?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the deep parts of the seas and waters.
medium.q: What are “deep places” in the context of verse 6?

answers: Nature is presented as subject to His absolute rule
Nature is presented as an independent power
Nature is presented as the work of idols
medium.explanation: The LORD does whatsoever He pleases throughout all parts of creation.
medium.q: How does the description of nature support the theme of the LORD’s greatness?

answers: From Israel’s praise to criticism of the priests
From declaring the LORD’s greatness to examples of His rule over nature
From dividing the land to the Exodus
challenge.explanation: The passage first declares the LORD’s greatness and then describes His works in creation.

answers: That the LORD’s rule is limited to one place
That His rule extends throughout all creation
That the sea is more important than the earth
challenge.explanation: The list presents the LORD’s authority over every part of creation.
challenge.q: What does the mention of heaven, earth, seas, and deep places teach?

challenge.explanation: The giving of land to Israel appears later in the psalm, not in verses 6–7.
challenge.q: Which action is not mentioned in verses 6–7?

paragraphs.title: The LORD’s Greatness in History and Israel’s Victory

easy.explanation: Verse 8 says He smote the firstborn of Egypt, both man and beast.
easy.q: Whom did the LORD smite in Egypt?

answers: Against Pharaoh and all his servants
easy.explanation: Verse 9 mentions Pharaoh and all his servants.
easy.q: Against whom did the LORD send tokens and wonders?

answers: The lands of the kings for an inheritance
easy.explanation: Verse 12 says He gave their land for an heritage unto Israel His people.
easy.q: What did the LORD give to Israel?

answers: The plagues of Egypt, the defeat of kings, and the giving of their land to Israel
Building the temple, offering sacrifices, and going into captivity
Creating the world, making man, and blessing the priests
medium.explanation: The passage moves from Egypt to defeated kings and finally to Israel’s inheritance.
medium.q: What sequence is described in verses 8–12?

medium.explanation: In this context, an heritage is land given to a people as an inheritance.

answers: Defeating the kings made it possible for Israel to receive their lands
The inheritance caused the plagues in Egypt
The victories ended Israel’s special calling
medium.explanation: After describing the defeated kings, the psalm says their land was given to Israel.
medium.q: How are the LORD’s victories and Israel’s inheritance related?

answers: That the victory included particular kings as well as all the kingdoms of Canaan
That they were servants of Pharaoh
That they were priests in Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: Verses 10–11 name Sihon, Og, and all the kingdoms of Canaan among the defeated rulers.
challenge.q: What does the mention of Sihon and Og emphasize?

answers: Both reveal the LORD’s power against enemies
challenge.explanation: The passage presents the LORD’s actions in Egypt and in battle as demonstrations of His greatness.
challenge.q: What connection is made between the plagues of Egypt and Israel’s wars?

challenge.explanation: The psalm describes the LORD as the One who smote nations and slew mighty kings.
challenge.q: To whom are the acts of smiting the nations and kings attributed?

paragraphs.title: The Enduring Name of the LORD and His Judgment

answers: Until the end of the war
easy.explanation: Verse 13 says, “Thy name, O LORD, endureth for ever.”
easy.q: How long does the name of the LORD endure?

easy.explanation: The verse says the LORD’s memorial continues throughout all generations.
Verse 14 says, “the LORD will judge his people.”

answers: He may turn from punishment and show mercy
He will build a new city
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the LORD relenting toward His servants and showing compassion.
medium.q: What does “he will repent himself concerning his servants” mean in this passage?

answers: The rule of the kings of Canaan
medium.explanation: Verse 13 declares that the LORD’s name endures for ever and His memorial through all generations.
medium.q: What endures for ever according to the passage?

answers: He judges His people but may show mercy toward His servants
He pays no attention to His people
He delivers His people to idols
medium.explanation: The passage combines judgment with the possibility that the LORD will relent concerning His servants.
medium.q: How is the LORD’s treatment of His people described?

answers: Judgment upon the people and mercy toward the servants
The creation of heaven and the creation of earth
challenge.explanation: The verse speaks both of the LORD judging His people and of His relenting concerning His servants.

answers: The temporary nature of the LORD’s memorial
The continuing remembrance of the LORD through the generations
The LORD’s dependence upon earthly kings
challenge.explanation: The phrase stresses the lasting remembrance of the LORD from generation to generation.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “throughout all generations” emphasize?

answers: The LORD is eternal, and He continues to judge and show mercy to His people
The LORD disappears after judging His people
The LORD changes from Israel’s God to an idol
challenge.explanation: The enduring name of the LORD is joined with His continuing work of judgment and mercy.

paragraphs.title: The Powerlessness of Idols and the Blessing of the LORD’s Worshippers

easy.explanation: Verse 15 says the idols are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands.
easy.q: What are the idols of the heathen made of?

easy.explanation: Verses 16–17 say the idols have mouths, eyes, and ears but cannot speak, see, or hear.
easy.q: What can the idols not do?

answers: Israel, the house of Aaron, the house of Levi, and those who fear the LORD
Only the kings of the heathen
easy.explanation: Verses 19–20 call all these groups to bless the LORD.
easy.q: Who is called to bless the LORD?

answers: The images or statues of the nations
medium.explanation: The expression refers to the idols made by the nations.
medium.q: What does “the idols of the heathen” refer to?

answers: The ability to live and act
medium.explanation: Although they have mouths, eyes, and ears, they have no breath or power to act.
medium.q: What do the idols lack despite having bodily features?

answers: Israel, the house of Aaron, the house of Levi, and those who fear the LORD
The house of Levi, Egypt, Israel, and the house of Aaron
Those who fear the LORD, the kings of Canaan, Israel, and the nations
medium.explanation: This is the order given in verses 19–20.
medium.q: What is the order of the groups called to bless the LORD?

answers: Those who make and trust in idols become spiritually powerless like the idols
Those who worship idols receive Israel’s land
Those who make idols become priests
challenge.explanation: The statement warns that idol-makers and idol-trusters become like the lifeless objects they serve.
challenge.q: What does “They that make them are like unto them” mean in context?

answers: The LORD is living and active, while the idols are powerless and without breath
The LORD is made of silver, while the idols are made of spirit
The LORD belongs to the heathen, while the idols belong to Israel
challenge.explanation: The idols cannot speak, see, hear, or breathe, whereas the LORD acts throughout creation and history.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast between the LORD and the idols?

answers: From Zion, where He dwells at Jerusalem
From the sea toward the deep places
challenge.explanation: Verse 21 says, “Blessed be the LORD out of Zion, which dwelleth at Jerusalem.”
challenge.q: From where is the LORD blessed at the end of the psalm?
